description: Cycles, ecosystems, order, and the planet they happen on. Life itself is in life.json.

concepts.title: Nature
concepts.summary: Rivers branching. Seasons turning. Something growing where something else fell. Nature isn't always gentle, but it keeps a rhythm much bigger than the noise in my head.

concepts.title: Cycles
concepts.summary: Water rises, falls, and rises again. Carbon passes from air to leaf to soil. Matter is reused; only energy moves one way through.

concepts.title: Seasons
concepts.summary: Earth's tilt, carried around the Sun, tips each hemisphere toward and away from the light. The whole living world keeps time with it: leaves, migrations, moods, festivals.

concepts.title: Carbon Cycle
concepts.summary: Carbon moves from air into plants, from plants into animals and soil, and back to air through breath and fire. Burning fossil fuels moves it faster than the rest of the cycle can absorb.

concepts.title: Water
concepts.summary: Rain, river, ocean, cloud, breath. Water shapes stone slowly and life quickly, and it holds patience better than anything else I know.

concepts.title: Water Cycle
concepts.summary: The Sun lifts water from the sea, wind carries it inland, and it falls, gathers, and runs back down. Every glass of water has taken part in it many times before.

concepts.title: Ecosystems
concepts.summary: Nothing lives alone. Fungi trade with roots, predators shape the meadow, and a fallen tree feeds a hundred neighbors. The web matters more than any single strand.

concepts.title: Part of Nature
concepts.summary: It's easy to talk as if we stood outside nature, looking in. We don't. Our bodies are ecosystems, our cities are habitats, and our attention is shaped by the same weather.

concepts.title: Symbiosis
concepts.summary: Different species living closely together, often each depending on the other. Lichens, gut bacteria, and the mitochondria in your cells are all partnerships so old they've become single things.

concepts.title: Food Webs
concepts.summary: Who eats whom, tangled into a web instead of a chain. Energy from the Sun thins out at each step, which is why there are far more plants than predators.

concepts.title: Biodiversity
concepts.summary: The variety of living things in a place. A rich mix makes an ecosystem resilient, because when one species falters another can fill its role.

concepts.title: Fungi
concepts.summary: Neither plants nor animals, and closer to animals than plants. Most of a fungus is a hidden mesh of threads that breaks down the dead and links the roots of living trees.

concepts.title: Peace
concepts.summary: Sometimes peace is stillness, sometimes balance, sometimes just acceptance. In a forest it's less the absence of activity than the absence of demand.

concepts.title: Order
concepts.summary: Not design, but repetition. Simple rules, run over and over under steady pressure, leave patterns behind. Snowflakes, dunes, honeycomb: order that nobody planned and everybody can see.

concepts.title: Patterns
concepts.summary: Branching rivers and branching lungs. Spirals in shells and in galaxies. Similar constraints keep arriving at similar shapes, so nature repeats itself because the problems repeat.

concepts.title: Earth
concepts.summary: A small rocky planet at the right distance from an ordinary star, with liquid water, a magnetic field, and an atmosphere thin enough to see through. So far it's the only place we know that life has found.

concepts.title: Plate Tectonics
concepts.summary: The planet's surface is a jigsaw of slowly moving plates. Where they collide mountains rise, where they part oceans open, and where they grind, earthquakes strike.

concepts.title: Atmosphere
concepts.summary: A thin layer of gas, mostly nitrogen and oxygen, that holds in warmth, blocks harmful rays, and carries weather. Seen from orbit it's a fine blue line barely thicker than a coat of paint.

concepts.title: Oceans
concepts.summary: Most of the planet's surface, and most of its living space. They store heat, move it around the globe, and hold far more of the world's carbon than the air does.

concepts.title: Climate
concepts.summary: Weather averaged over decades. It's set by sunlight, the atmosphere, oceans, and ice, and it now shifts because people have changed how much heat the atmosphere holds.

concepts.title: Weather
concepts.summary: The atmosphere on a given day: sunlight heats the ground unevenly, air rises and sinks, moisture condenses. It's chaotic, which is why forecasts fade after a week or so.

concepts.title: Lightning
concepts.summary: Charge builds up inside storm clouds until the air itself gives way and a channel of current tears through it. The flash heats the air to hotter than the surface of the Sun.
